verdict.rationale: Convex provides its own non-production environments: a dev deployment that CLI pushes and runs target, local deployments for development, and preview deployments. Its MCP server is blocked from production by default specifically to prevent accidental changes to production data. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that dev, preview and local deployment data is fully isolated from production; any independent or hands-on corroboration of the sandbox workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: By default, the MCP server cannot access production deployments. This is a safety measure to prevent accidental modifications to production data.
Run a public or internal Convex query, mutation, or action on your development deployment.
It's also possible to run a Convex deployment locally for development.
When you change a function or the schema, the new versions are pushed to your dev deployment
